attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - Candidate claims hydrogen is kept below 25% of LEL "by the turbulent ballast flow and the existing natural tank venting" during a 3-log chlorination at 8-10 mg/L TRO for 4 h, but H2 evolution from in-line electrolysis at that TRO dose occurs concurrently with ballast uptake (slug flow, partially filled tanks, stratified headspace) so turbulence is intermittent and buoyancy-driven stratification in dead zones is the dominant transport, not turbulent mixing; the candidate's own listed failure mode ("hydrogen stratification in tank headspace dead zones") confirms the mechanism the design relies on is the very one that fails.
attacks.weak_transfer: KILLED - Transfers the lab/bench assumption of well-mixed, vented single-phase flow to ship ballast uptake where tanks fill sequentially at ~150-2000 m3/h with the free surface and ullage present throughout most of the 4 h dwell, so the "turbulent dilution" element fails to transfer to the actual two-phase filling regime.
attacks.engineering_infeasibility: KILLED - At 8-10 mg/L TRO dosing in seawater with ~100% current efficiency for H2, ~1.3-1.6 m3 H2 per m3 ballast is generated; even with an existing Pv vent sized for thermal/pressure breathing only (typically a few m3/h), the candidate's "stay below 25% LEL by dilution" requires venting rates orders of magnitude above the stated Pv vent capacity at the upper-bound 10 mg/L case, which the design does not provide.
